analysis.title: Phillips 66 (PSX) Investor Group Lunch/3Q Recap: Positive Rate of Change on Refining, Balance Sheet Strength & Capital Returns
key_insights: GS hosted PSX VP of Investor Relations and Chief Economist Sean Maher in NYC on 11/4 after 3Q26 earnings. Takeaways: constructive global refining supply/demand, a clear Midstream earnings growth path, unchanged capital allocation priorities (buybacks and debt paydown), and steps to improve the commercial capability of the refining system.

GS keeps a Neutral rating and a $297 price target (6-month, SOTP and 13.0x P/E on normalized EPS). It sees risk/reward improving from deleveraging, better refining operations and supportive non-refining earnings. Price is $259.63, implying 14.4% upside.

Management says about 7 mb/d of global refining capacity remains offline across Russia, Asia and the Middle East, causing significant market dislocation. U.S. gasoline demand is down about 2.5% and diesel about 1.5%, but management says the demand response is not enough to balance the market.

Management expects wider WCS-WTI differentials to persist. Strong global diesel margins push refiners to pull forward WTI to backfill displaced grades, while high freight rates and Venezuelan barrels pressure heavy crude pricing. Freight rates are projected higher in 4Q than 3Q, with possible further increases next year.

PSX imports more Canadian crude into the U.S. than any peer, so its Central Corridor and Gulf Coast assets benefit most from wider light-heavy differentials. Each $1 of WCS-WTI widening is worth about $140 mn of earnings to PSX.

PSX has chartered more than 40 ships and has 40 more time-charter ships scheduled over the next 2.5 years. Charter costs are below current rates, which gives the refining business a structural cost advantage.
PSX reported a 41% distillate yield in 3Q. Management says its Atlantic Basin facilities can push distillate yields to 43%-44%.

Midstream has strong asset utilization and a growing project backlog: Permian processing via the Iron Mesa and Zeus gas plants, Coastal Bend NGL pipeline expansion, a third Corpus Christi fractionator targeted for 2028, and Western Gateway. These support a target of about 5% annual Midstream EBITDA growth through the decade.

Capital allocation: PSX targets returning at least 50% of adjusted net operating cash flow to shareholders. It returned $2.8 bn in 3Q26 (about 45% payout) and expects returns above 50% in 4Q to reach a full-year target of about 50%.

PSX cut debt by about $2 bn in 3Q and addressed a $500 mn October maturity. Total debt is about $18 bn against a $17 bn target. Management sees a clear path to the target in 2027 while keeping flexibility for early repayment or opportunistic buybacks.

GS raised its 2026-2028 EPS estimates to $35.18/$30.23/$21.37 from $30.79/$28.69/$21.13 and its 4Q EPS estimate is $11.20 versus FactSet consensus of $11.01. GS lowered the refining EV/EBITDA multiple in its SOTP from 5.5x to 5.0x to reflect energy market multiples, leaving the price target unchanged.
GS lists key risks as refining margins, operational execution and chemicals earnings.

market_movers.rationale: Neutral and $297 target unchanged after 3Q26 results. GS sees improving risk/reward from deleveraging, refining operations and Midstream growth, with estimates raised and the refining multiple cut to 5.0x.

sector_views.rationale: Management and GS describe a constructive backdrop of constrained global refining capacity, relatively stable demand and favorable crude differentials.

earnings_insights: PSX 3Q26 results were reported before this note (reported 3Q26, company data). The company reported a 41% distillate yield in 3Q and returned $2.8 bn to shareholders in 3Q26 (about 45% payout).
GS 4Q26 EPS estimate is $11.20 versus FactSet consensus of $11.01 (both estimates, not printed). PSX has not yet reported 4Q.
GS 2026E/2027E/2028E diluted EPS (pre-exceptionals) is $35.18/$30.23/$21.37 (GS estimates), up from $30.79/$28.69/$21.13 previously. GS 2025 diluted EPS pre-exceptionals was $6.47 (actual).
GS 2026E-2028E revenue estimates are $178,986 mn, $167,303 mn and $156,847 mn (GS estimates), and 2026E EBITDA is $21,728 mn on the cover table, versus $8,363 mn for 2025 (actual).
Management expects capital returns to exceed 50% of adjusted net operating cash flow in 4Q to reach the full-year target of about 50%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Management observed slight domestic contraction in gasoline demand but says the demand response is insufficient to balance the market.
Slight contraction in diesel demand, while global diesel margins stay strong.
Capacity offline across Russia, Asia and the Middle East continues to cause significant market dislocation.
Management expects wide differentials to persist. Each $1 of widening is about $140 mn of earnings for PSX.

macro_indicators.reading: higher in 4Q vs. 3Q, potentially higher into next year
macro_indicators.interpretation: Higher freight pressures heavy crude pricing including WCS, which widens differentials.

geopolitical: About 7 mb/d of refining capacity remains offline across Russia, Asia and the Middle East, per management.
Venezuelan barrels continue to exert downward pressure on heavy-crude pricing, including WCS.
